solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Former French PM, and member, plugging in a decorative novelty item

indicators.note: plugging in says the PM and member together close round the next word, as a plug fills a hole

parts.note: Pierre Laval was twice Prime Minister of France in the 1930s
MP, Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A disgraced French premier and a legislator wiring up a quirky ornament.
explanation.walkthrough: Pierre Laval led the French government in the 1930s and under Vichy. 'Plugging in' sounds electrical, fitting a lamp, but places the 'a' between his name and the member.
explanation.definitionFit: The bubbling wax lamp is a classic 1960s ornamental gimmick, a decorative novelty.

clue.text: Communion table set up in minster, at last

indicators.note: set up says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: The communion table has finally been erected in the cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft lacked the word 'in', which signals the concealed run; added as its indicator. In a down clue 'set up' means read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: In churches the table at which Communion is celebrated is called the altar.

clue.text: Suitable nick

definitions.meaning: to steal, British slang; the verb meaning to take for oneself

explanation.definitionFit: One spelling is both an adjective meaning fitting and a verb meaning to take, which is what nick means in British slang.

clue.text: A noble lady's describing plot for novel

indicators.note: describing in crosswords means drawing a line round, so the noble lady wraps the plot

parts.note: a dame is a woman with a title of honour
a bed is a plot of garden ground

explanation.surface: A titled woman outlines the storyline of a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Describing' is used in its geometric sense of tracing around. 'Plot' looks like a story outline, but is a garden plot.
explanation.definitionFit: George Eliot's first full-length work of fiction, published 1859, bears this title.

clue.text: Leading family members in promotion of goodwill

parts.note: public in the loose sense of prominent, out in front of everyone
relations are relatives

explanation.surface: Prominent kinsfolk taking part in a goodwill campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading' for public is loose: prominent, in the public eye.
explanation.definitionFit: PR is the profession of building favourable opinion of an organisation among customers and the press.

clue.text: Get out of prison early in the year

definitions.meaning: to free someone from jail, a verb
the season from March to May, roughly

explanation.definitionFit: To free a convict is a slang verb, and the first season of the calendar follows winter.

clue.text: Very old article brings comfort

parts.note: very means so, as in so tired
the definite article

explanation.surface: An ancient piece of writing provides solace.
explanation.definitionFit: To calm or console someone is to bring them comfort; both are verbs in third person.

clue.text: Diamond, perhaps cut for fabulous bird

indicators.note: cut means the word is docked of its final letter

parts.note: rock is slang for a gemstone, a diamond being an example

explanation.surface: A gem, maybe, is shaped for a legendary bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' looks like the jeweller's work on a diamond, but it shortens the slang word by its last letter, K.
explanation.definitionFit: In Arabian legend the giant bird that carried off elephants appears in the Sinbad tales.

clue.text: Awfully mean celebrities — say who they are

indicators.note: awfully suggests the letters of mean are badly treated and rearranged

parts.note: big names are famous people

explanation.surface: Nasty famous people: reveal their identities!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awfully' rearranges MEAN to NAME.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to identify those involved, especially informers listing accomplices.

clue.text: More work wanted

parts.note: Sir Thomas More wrote a book about an ideal island society, a place everyone would want

explanation.walkthrough: Reads as a request for extra labour, but More is Sir Thomas More, whose 1516 book named this perfect imagined state.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas More's famous treatise depicts an ideal, desirable commonwealth.

clue.text: Centre for juvenile offenders affected by return of further bishop

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: return of says the word for further is turned back

parts.note: too means also, in addition
camp means mannered or affected

explanation.surface: A youth detention centre swayed by a cleric coming back again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Affected' looks like a past participle but is the adjective camp; 'return of' turns the word for further backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A short, harsh, military-style regime for young offenders is called this.

clue.text: City in the Czech Republic showing Born Free?

indicators.note: free here means the letters are set loose and rearranged

explanation.surface: Asks if a Czech city appears in the film Born Free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Born Free' looks like the lion film title; 'Free' rearranges BORN.
explanation.definitionFit: Moravia's chief town is the second largest city in the Czech Republic.

clue.text: Foolish, thoughtlessly indifferent group

parts.note: blithe means carelessly unconcerned
a ring is a group of people, such as a spy ring

explanation.surface: A gang that is stupid and casually uncaring.
explanation.definitionFit: A British colloquial intensifier for idiotic, as in a blithering idiot.

clue.text: Story is sexy, they say

parts.note: a rumour is a story going round
to have it, or it, is to have sex appeal

explanation.surface: Gossip that something is alluring, so people claim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' is old slang for sex appeal, so someone sexy has it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase introduces hearsay, the same as saying people claim it.

clue.text: Live rough abroad, on river, with dog

parts.note: L marks the live terminal in electrical wiring

indicators.note: rough means roughly handled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Sleeping rough overseas by a river, with a canine companion.
explanation.walkthrough: L for live comes from electrical plugs, where the terminals are marked L, N and E; 'rough' rearranges abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: A popular breed of retriever originally from Newfoundland.

clue.text: Nursemaid brings in a ring for religious leader

indicators.note: brings in means the nursemaid's letters enclose the other piece

parts.note: an ayah is a nursemaid in India
an atoll is a ring of coral

explanation.surface: A nanny arrives with a ring meant for a cleric.
explanation.walkthrough: An ayah is an Indian nursemaid, a word from the British Raj; 'a ring' is one piece, a coral reef shaped like a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior Shia Muslim cleric in Iran holds this title.

clue.text: I am contracted in Maine to produce a play without dialogue

indicators.note: in puts the shortened pronoun inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: ME is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Maine
I am shortened gives I'm

explanation.surface: Someone signed up in Maine to stage a silent performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contracted' looks like signing a contract; it means shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: A wordless dramatic performance using gesture alone is the meaning here.

clue.text: Beneath one, DI faring badly

indicators.note: badly signals the letters are jumbled out of order

explanation.surface: A Detective Inspector doing poorly is undignified.
explanation.walkthrough: DI is a Detective Inspector in British police.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin-derived phrase means below one's dignity, unbecoming.

clue.text: Flag associated with a roman- fleuve?

parts.note: to flag is to droop or tire, which is to sag; the answer also runs backwards across 'Flag associated', a coincidence the setter did not use

explanation.surface: Asks if a banner is linked to a long novel.
explanation.walkthrough: A roman-fleuve is a long multi-volume novel tracing a family.
explanation.definitionFit: A long family chronicle in several novels, like Galsworthy's Forsyte books.

clue.text: Suffer deprivation in Libya's capital, and mental torture

indicators.note: capital means the first letter, the capital letter of the word

parts.note: anguish is severe mental pain

explanation.surface: Enduring hardship in Tripoli together with psychological agony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Libya's capital' looks like Tripoli but is just its first letter, L.
explanation.definitionFit: To pine or waste away from lack of something is to suffer deprivation.

clue.text: Creamy dessert — seconds accepted by timid type

indicators.note: accepted by puts the seconds abbreviation inside the timid person

parts.note: a mouse is a shy, timid person

explanation.surface: A shy person takes a second helping of pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seconds' suggests a second helping, but means S.
explanation.definitionFit: A light whipped chocolate or fruit pudding is a creamy dessert.

clue.text: Man responsible for standards in small firm, left journalist right away

parts.note: Co is the short form of company

indicators.note: away says the letter for right is taken off

parts.note: a reporter is a journalist

explanation.surface: A boss of a small company left a reporter at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standards' are jazz and song standards, not principles; 'away' drops R, leaving EPORTER.
explanation.definitionFit: The American composer wrote many songs now regarded as classics of the Great American Songbook.

clue.text: Conceal Welsh identity, to some degree

indicators.note: to some degree says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Keeping one's nationality from Wales partly secret.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep something out of sight is to conceal it; both are verbs.

clue.text: Lament what's dreadful about opening in game

indicators.note: about means the word for dreadful goes round the other letter

parts.note: dire means dreadful

indicators.note: opening in picks the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Bemoaning something terrible about the start of a match.
explanation.definitionFit: A mournful funeral song or elegy is a lament.

clue.text: Caught wearing scruffy loafers outside

indicators.note: wearing means the rearranged shoes surround the letter
scruffy says the letters are untidy, so rearranged

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone spotted in shabby slip-on shoes out of doors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scruffy' rearranges LOAFERS to ALFRESO; 'wearing' puts C inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian phrase means in the open air, as in eating outdoors.

clue.text: Manage to stand

definitions.meaning: to be in charge of or operate
to stand as a candidate in an election

explanation.definitionFit: One verb means both to operate a business and to be a candidate for office.

clue.text: Leave course, having lost heart

indicators.note: having lost heart says one middle letter is dropped

parts.note: dessert is a course of a meal

explanation.surface: Quitting a training course after becoming discouraged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' is a meal course, not a study one; one of DESSERT's central S's goes.
explanation.definitionFit: To abandon someone or something is to leave them.

clue.text: Convert put to death in church

indicators.note: in puts the execution word inside the church letters

parts.note: CE is Church of England
to hang is to execute

explanation.surface: A religious convert executed inside a church.
explanation.definitionFit: To alter or transform something is to convert it; both are verbs.

clue.text: Visit places of interest, two spots

parts.note: to spot is to catch sight of, sight as a verb
to spot is also to see

explanation.surface: Touring the attractions at a couple of locations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spots' looks like a noun for places, but is two verbs meaning notices.
explanation.definitionFit: To tour the famous landmarks of a place is to go on a tourist round.
